# Cases shared by the Rust code (tags.rs) and the editor (web/tagrules.js).
# "name <text> => yes|no" says whether the text is a tag name (without the #).
# "find <text> => tag, tag" lists the tags in a page text, in order. In <text>, \n is a line
# break, \t a tab and \\ a backslash.

name plan => yes
name Plan_2 => yes
name project/alpha => yes
name to-do => yes
name 1984 => no
name 1984a => yes
name y1984 => yes
name 2024-11 => yes
name 12/34 => yes
name é => yes
name Ünï/ça => yes
name 日本語 => yes
name a.b => no
name a b => no
name  => no
name a#b => no
name - => yes
name _ => yes

find Hello #plan today => plan
find #plan at the start => plan
find line one\n#second line => second
find two #a #b #c => a, b, c
find tab\t#a => a
find end of #tag. next => tag
find end of #tag, next => tag
find a#b => (none)
find word#tag #real => real
find # heading => (none)
find ## heading => (none)
find ##tag => (none)
find #1984 and #2024 => (none)
find #y1984 => y1984
find #a/b/c nested => a/b/c
find #é and #日本語 => é, 日本語
find `#code` and #real => real
find ``#code`` #real => real
find unclosed ` #still a tag => still
find ```\n#fenced\n```\n#after => after
find ~~~\n#fenced\n~~~\n#after => after
find http://example.local/#frag => (none)
find (#a) and "#b" => (none)
find \\#escaped #real => real
find [[Page#Heading]] #real => real
find [[Page #Heading]] #real => real
find ![[Pic]] #real => real
find [[ #a => a
find [text](#anchor) #real => real
find #Plan and #plan => Plan, plan
find #a#b => a
find #a-#b => a-
